dossier.public_summary: The dip changes dramatically between sectors and between individual transits, with some transits showing twice the depth and one showing no dip at all. Odd and even dips differ and a second dip appears, which together point to noise or a blended binary, not a planet on this star.

reasons.why: Depth changes by factor of ~239 across sectors. Sector depths: 2721, -394, 2755 ppm vs QLP 6565 ppm (chi2 186.8 dof 3)
Changes persist within the same light-curve product, not just between QLP and SPOC: real depth changes, not calibration. Per-sector 2721 to -394 ppm shows non-transit variation.
Individual transits inconsistent. Signal driven by ~3 deep outliers (901 of SNR from top 3) and a negative depth (-890 ppm) and near-zero (7 ppm), inconsistent with a planet.
reasons.value: p_consistent 1.2464910946336229e-58 share_of_top_3 0.901 top outliers 5502 ppm sigma 9.1, 6565 ppm sigma 8.7, -890 ppm sigma -7.9

reasons.why: Odd and even depths differ strongly by 1113 ppm, favouring a binary at twice the period (28.6 d). Combined with a secondary SNR 5.998 depth_ppm 846.9 (depth_over_dip 0.4066) this supports an eclipsing binary/false alarm over a planet.
Centroid inconclusive and no neighbour within 1px can cause the dip, but depth-instability and odd/even+secondary provide positive evidence the signal is not a planet on target.
